newsitem.title: USA: Republicans, Democrats grumble over subpoenas.
newsitem.headline: Republicans, Democrats grumble over subpoenas.

text.p: Congressional investigators from both parties griped publicly Tuesday that they were not getting cooperation on subpoenas in the probes of campaign fund-raising abuses.

The lead investigator in the House, Indiana Republican Dan Burton, who is chairman of the Committee on Government Reform and Oversight, went to the House floor to charge that President Clinton was employing "dilatory practices" and not answering subpoenas for documents.
These included requests for information involving former Democratic fund-raiser John Huang and the Riady family, which heads the giant Lippo Group Indonesian banking organisation.

Huang, a Chinese-born naturalised American, is a former Commerce Department employee and one-time executive of Lippo. Riady family members are friends of Clinton and linked to the fund-raising controversy.
Among the allegations are that foreign money was given illegally in the 1996 election to win favours, with most of the charges involving Clinton's Democrats.

In the Senate, Ohio's John Glenn, senior Democrat on the Governmental Affairs Committee, wrote to the Republican chairman, Sen. Fred Thompson of Tennessee, to complain that draft subpoenas proposed by Democrats for information about Republican fund-raising activities were not being considered.

He said nearly 90 Republican-initiated subpoenas for information about Democrats had gone out with "minimal delay" but that "the same cannot be said of subpoenas regarding Republican fund-raising requested by the minority."
Glenn asked for a public hearing to air the dispute over the documents. There was no immediate reply from Thompson.

Some of the information requests cited by Burton in the House involve Huang, who has pleaded his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination and refused to cooperate with investigators. Burton said the requests involving Huang and the Riady family were first made over six months ago.
His floor speech followed his charge in a statement Monday that his committee was being "stonewalled" since the White House had missed a noon deadline Monday to produce the Huang and Riady material.

Burton accused Clinton of "repeating the same dilatory practices of the past" when the committee sought documents regarding the Whitewater land deal and an investigation on FBI personnel files obtained by the White House.

He said many of the documents sought by the committee in its campaign funds probe "pertain to close friends that the president has appointed to high goverment positions, such as Webster Hubbell, John Huang and Mark Middleton."

Hubbell, a former top Justice Department official who went to jail for defrauding his former Little Rock law firm where he was a partner with Hillary Clinton, and Middleton, a former White House aide, also have refused to cooperate with the committee on Fifth Amendment grounds.

Other documents Burton sought included records involving Charles Yah Lin Trie, a one-time Little Rock restaurant owner and friend of the president as well as a Democratic fund-raiser who has left the country.
